title: 第1章 肥羊第2章 老骗子与小杂毛
content_zh:
第1章肥羊
又是一年府试的时候，还不到卯时，天色还未大亮，梁州西平府的贡院考棚外面就挤满了各种各样的人。既有维持秩序的胥吏公差，有送考的家人亲属，又有看热闹的路人街坊，还有随行的仆人小厮，热热闹闹的足有数千人。
当然数量最多的还是形色各异的考生，有胸有成竹意气风发的学子，有懵懂无知亦步亦趋的初试孩童，也有沉着冷静默不作声的考场老手，甚至还有须发皆白仍心存幻想的老学究。
所有这些人之中，无论是心中焦躁的，还是故作漫不经心的，又或者是正与他人高谈阔论的，无一例外的都随时注意着贡院的大门。一年就这么一次机会，马上就要开始了，可不能耽搁了正事。
整个现场只有一个人对此并不在意，而是左顾右盼，在人群之中来回穿梭，似乎在寻找着下手的机会。这是一个十五六岁的少年，一件不太合身的破旧道袍披在身上，面目清秀，身材略显瘦削，一双大眼睛似乎充满灵气，让人望而心生亲近之意。
忽然，他似乎发现了下手的目标，径直往前走了几步，来到一个穿着富贵的肥胖书生面前，稽首道：“小道青阳有礼了。”
那肥胖的书生旁边还跟着一个斜眉吊眼的下人，看到有人挡在前面，伸手推搡道：“去去去，别挡了我们进场的道路，若是耽搁了我们家少爷考试，你一个破道士可是吃罪不起。”
好不容易遇到一个大肥羊，岂能就这么让他跑了？小道士青阳站在原地没动，就这么看着那肥胖书生。
那肥胖书生对小道士青阳倒没有什么成见，斜着眼睛看了看他半天，说道：“你为何拦住我的去路？”
小道士青阳从怀中掏出一张黄色的符箓，拿在手里说道：“我看这位公子才气冲天，富贵逼人，一定是出自名门世家。这里有一张灵运符，正适合公子这样的身份地位，这张灵符可以增加主人的气运，保佑主人心想事成，只需要五十枚大钱就能请到。”
增加气运，心想事成？世上哪有这么好的事？旁边那下人又站出来道：“你个小骗子，坑蒙拐骗居然骗到我们家少爷身上了，再不滚，信不信我把你扭送官府？”
眼看着那下人就要动手，那肥胖书生一把拉住了他，转身对着小道士青阳道：“这灵符真的能增加气运，保佑我心想事成？”
被那下人喝骂，小道士青阳原以为这笔生意要泡汤，听了肥胖书生的话，顿时喜出望外，连忙道：“那是当然，这灵符是我师父松鹤真人耗费了七七四十九天才炼制而成的，灵验无比，童叟无欺。”
得到小道士青阳的确认，那肥胖书生也是面带喜色，伸手接过林阳的那张灵符贴身藏好，然后冲着自己那下人使了个眼色，让他付钱。那下人是一百个不相信灵符有用，可看少爷的心思，知道不买不成，于是心不甘情不愿的掏出五十枚大钱扔给了青阳。
这笔生意这么容易就做成了，小道士青阳准备再接再厉，从怀中又掏出一枚粗陋的玉符，然后向前迈了一小步，低声道：“除了那张灵符，我还有一件更好的宝物，就是这枚状元符。只要得到了这枚玉符，保你在以后的考试中才思敏捷，下笔如有神助，场场高中，就算成为状元也不是不可能的。”
那肥胖书生似乎有些心动，道：“这玉符多少钱？”
小道士青阳伸出两根手指头，道：“这状元符我只收你一个成本价，二两银子！不是我狮子大开口，实在是这枚状元符太过贵重，这是我师父松鹤真人耗费了好几年的功夫才炼制而成的，开光之后又在三清祖师的面前供奉了几十年，整个梁州也就这么一块儿，价值连城，要真卖便宜了，也不符合您的身份不是？”
小道士青阳侃侃而谈，那肥胖书生眉头却是皱着眉头，冷哼一声，道：“你当我是真傻？对于本少爷来说，五十枚大钱根本就不算什么，我买你那灵符，纯粹就是想要讨个好彩头，结果你还可这我一个人坑，真是岂有此理。滚，趁着本少爷还没有发火，赶快滚。”
旁边那下人早就看小道士不顺眼了，这时终于找到了发作的机会，一把把青阳推了个趔趄，恶狠狠的道：“你个小杂毛，再不滚，我可动手了。”
看到对方翻脸，小道士青阳明白只能到此为之了，这种事他也不知道经历过多少回了，于是嘿嘿一笑，就转身离开了人群，朝着下一个目标走去。

只不过钻出人群之后，小道士青阳的手上已经多了一块半两重的碎银子，见到街边的的一群乞丐，他随手就把那块碎银扔了出去，那群乞丐显然没有料到有人会如此大方，抓起那块碎银一哄而散。
这是他临走前施展妙手空空的手段，从那下人身上得到的，敢推我，道爷就让你破财。青阳的师父松鹤老道浪迹江湖游戏风尘，劫富济贫做过不少，坑蒙拐骗也是家常便饭，行事亦正亦邪，青阳从小受到师父的影响，做这样的事情没有是丝毫理负担。
卯时一刻，考生开始进入考棚，外面的人才逐渐的稀疏起来，等到日上三竿，考生们进场完毕，就连看热闹的人都陆陆续续的离去，小道士青阳彻底的没了生意。
只是这种骗钱的机会可遇而不可求，院士也是一年才有这么一次，下次也不知到什么时候了。他摸了摸自己的怀里，这次带来的十几张灵符都卖光了，五块玉符只卖出去了一块，不过总体来说，收入还算不错，至少师父今年的酒钱是够了。
他扭头看了看身后的贡院，这才依依不舍的出了府城。为了赚这点钱，小道士青阳昨天下午就出发来到了府城，在贡院外面的街上露宿了一夜，眼看着太阳越来越高，若是不走快一点，中午都到不了家。
小道士青阳和师父松鹤真人相依为命，两个人住在府城外面不远处一座小山后面的小道观里，距离府城并不是太远，只是山路崎岖难行，步行至少需要一个多时辰。
（本章完）
content_en:
Chapter 1 Fat Sheep
It’s the time for the annual government examination again. It’s not even midnight yet, and the sky is still dark. The outside of the Gongyuan examination shed in Xiping Prefecture, Liangzhou is crowded with all kinds of people. There were minor officials on duty to maintain order, family members and relatives taking exams, passers-by and neighbors watching the excitement, and servants and servants accompanying them. Thousands of people were busy.
Of course, the largest number of candidates are all kinds of candidates, including confident and high-spirited students, ignorant and ignorant first-time children who follow suit, calm and silent exam veterans, and even old academics with white hair and beard who still have illusions.
Among all these people, whether they were anxious, pretending to be careless, or talking loudly with others, all of them, without exception, were always paying attention to the gate of Gongyuan. This opportunity only comes once a year, and it's about to start, so we can't delay the business.
There was only one person in the entire scene who didn't care about this. Instead, he looked left and right, walking back and forth among the crowd, as if looking for an opportunity to strike. This is a young man of fifteen or sixteen years old. He wears a worn-out Taoist robe that doesn't fit well. He has a delicate face and a slightly thin figure. His big eyes seem to be full of aura, which makes people feel close to him.
Suddenly, he seemed to have discovered his target. He walked a few steps forward and came to a fat scholar in rich clothes. He bowed his head and said, "Xiao Dao Qingyang is polite."
Next to the fat scholar was a servant with a squinting look. When he saw someone standing in front of him, he pushed him and said, "Go, go, don't block our way into the venue. If it delays our young master's exam, you, a broken Taoist priest, can't afford to suffer."
After finally meeting a big fat sheep, how could we just let him run away? The little Taoist priest Qingyang stood there without moving, just looking at the fat scholar.
The fat scholar didn't have any prejudice against the little Taoist Qingyang. He looked at him sideways for a long time and said, "Why are you blocking my way?"
The little Taoist priest Qingyang took out a yellow talisman from his arms, held it in his hand and said, "I think this young master is extremely talented and wealthy. He must come from a famous family. There is a lucky charm here, which is suitable for the young master's status. This magical charm can increase the master's luck and bless the master's wishes. You can get it with only fifty coins."
Increase your luck and make your wishes come true? How can there be such a good thing in the world? The servant next to him stood up again and said: "You little liar, you have deceived and deceived our young master. If you don't get out, believe it or not, I will take you to the government?"
Seeing that the man was about to take action, the fat scholar grabbed him, turned to the little Taoist Qingyang and said, "This talisman can really increase my luck and help my wishes come true?"
After being scolded by the servant, the young Taoist priest Qingyang thought that the business was going to be ruined. After hearing the fat scholar's words, he was overjoyed and said quickly: "Of course, this talisman was refined by my master Songhe Zhenren who spent 7749 days. It is extremely effective and can be used by children and old men alike."
After receiving the confirmation from the little Taoist Qingyang, the fat scholar also looked happy. He reached out to take Lin Yang's magic talisman and hid it close to his body. Then he winked at his servant and asked him to pay. The servant didn't believe that the magic talisman was useful, but looking at the young master's thoughts, he knew that it would be impossible if he didn't buy it, so he reluctantly took out fifty large coins and threw it to Qingyang.
The business was done so easily. The little Taoist Qingyang was ready to continue his efforts. He took out another crude jade talisman from his arms, then took a small step forward and whispered: "Besides that talisman, I have a better treasure, which is this number one talisman. As long as you get this jade talisman, you will be quick in thinking in future exams. If you have divine help in writing, it is not impossible to become the number one scholar in every high school."
The fat scholar seemed a little moved and said, "How much is this jade talisman?"money? "
The little Taoist priest Qingyang stretched out two fingers and said: "I will only charge you a cost price for this Number One Scholar Talisman, which is twenty taels of silver! It’s not that I’m a big talker, it’s just that this Number One Scholar Talisman is too precious. It took my master Songhe Zhenren several years of hard work to refine it. After it was consecrated, it was enshrined in front of the founder of the Sanqing Dynasty for decades. The entire Liangzhou is just like this. It’s priceless. If it’s really sold cheaply, it’s not in line with your status, isn’t it? "
The little Taoist Qingyang was talking eloquently, but the fat scholar frowned and snorted coldly, saying: "Do you think I am really stupid? To this young master, fifty pieces of money is nothing at all. I bought your magic talisman purely because I wanted to get a good fortune, but in the end, you still cheated me alone. It is really unreasonable. Get out, get out of here before this young master gets angry. "
The servant next to him had long disliked the little Taoist priest, and finally found an opportunity to attack. He pushed Qingyang to stagger and said viciously: "You little bastard, if you don't get out of here, I will do it." "
Seeing that the other party turned against him, the little Taoist Qingyang knew that this was the only way to go. He didn't know how many times he had experienced this kind of thing, so he smiled, turned around and left the crowd, heading towards the next target.
However, after getting out of the crowd, the little Taoist Qingyang already had a piece of broken silver weighing half a pound in his hand. When he saw a group of beggars on the street, he threw the piece of silver out. The group of beggars obviously did not expect that someone would be so generous. They grabbed the piece of silver and dispersed in a crowd.
This was a trick he used before leaving, and he got it from that servant. If you dare to push me, I will make you lose your fortune. Qingyang's master, Songhe Laodao, wandered around the world playing games, and did a lot of robbing the rich and helping the poor. Cheating and kidnapping were commonplace, and his actions were both good and evil. Qingyang was influenced by his master since he was a child, and he did not feel any burden to do such things.
At a quarter past two o'clock, the candidates began to enter the examination booth, and the number of people outside gradually became sparse. When the sun rose three o'clock, the candidates had entered the venue, and even the spectators left one after another. The little Taoist Qingyang completely lost his business.
It's just that this kind of opportunity to cheat money is rare. Academicians only get it once a year, and I don't know when the next time will be. He touched his arms. All the dozen or so spiritual talismans he brought this time were sold out, and only one of the five jade talismans was sold. But overall, the income was pretty good, at least the master had enough money for drinks this year.
He turned his head and looked at Gongyuan behind him, and then reluctantly left the city. In order to earn this little money, the young Taoist priest Qingyang set out for Fucheng yesterday afternoon and slept on the street outside Gongyuan all night. Seeing the sun getting higher and higher, if he didn't walk faster, he wouldn't be able to get home at noon.
The young Taoist priest Qingyang and his master Songhe Zhenren depended on each other. They lived in a small Taoist temple behind a hill not far from Fucheng. It was not too far from Fucheng, but the mountain road was rugged and difficult, and it took at least more than an hour to walk.
(End of chapter)
